streetView.conditionNotes: Roof appears to be in generally good condition with no obvious major defects visible from street-level view. Limited visibility due to angle and distance.
streetView.notes: This is a commercial/religious property (church), not a residential structure. The building features a brick facade with a white steeple and cross. The main sanctuary roof is a gable-style with what appears to be a secondary attached structure to the left (likely a fellowship hall or office wing). Roof slope is moderate pitch. Steeple roofing material and condition cannot be assessed from this angle. Low confidence on material type due to limited roof plane visibility from street-level perspective. A ladder inspection or aerial imagery would be required for accurate assessment. Estimating may need to account for steeple flashing and any roof penetrations not visible from this view.

satellite.notes: The roof is a complex hip/cross-hip configuration with a large primary hip mass and a secondary hip wing projecting from the northeast. Total interior linear footage sums to 186 ft, which falls within the expected sanity-check range of 132–192 ft for 6 facets. Ridge proportion is 46/186 = ~25%, consistent with a hip-dominant roof. Shadow patterns confirm sloped planes on all sides with no visible gable ends. One small vent cap visible on the main field. No visible damage, staining, or debris. Minimal tree encroachment on the north edge.
